b2-11-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Different Past
b2-11-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what would be different today if you had stayed in South Africa. You say you would not be living in Budapest.
b2-11-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what would be different if you had stayed in South Africa.
cues: Say what you would have done in the past
Say what would be different now
b2-11-01.target: Si me hubiera quedado en Sudáfrica, ahora no viviría en Budapest.
b2-11-01.english: If I had stayed in South Africa, I would not be living in Budapest now.
b2-11-01.canDo: I can say how a different past would change the present with si hubiera and the simple conditional.

b2-11-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Lasting Trait
b2-11-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos tells you he missed the bus again this morning. You say that he would not have missed it if he were less absent-minded.
b2-11-02.prompt: Tell Carlos that he would not have missed the bus if he were less absent-minded.
cues: Name the trait that would be different
Say what would not have happened
b2-11-02.target: Si fueras menos despistado, no habrías perdido el autobús.
b2-11-02.english: If you were less absent-minded, you would not have missed the bus.
b2-11-02.canDo: I can say how a lasting trait would have changed a past event with si + imperfect subjunctive and habría + participle.

b2-11-03.title: Communicative Challenge: On One Condition
b2-11-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks to borrow your computer. You agree on one condition: he must bring it back tonight.
b2-11-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that he can borrow your computer and on what condition.
cues: Say that you lend it to him
b2-11-03.target: Te presto la computadora siempre y cuando me la devuelvas esta noche.
b2-11-03.english: I will lend you the computer as long as you give it back to me tonight.
b2-11-03.canDo: I can set a strict condition with siempre y cuando and con la condición de que.

b2-11-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Except If
b2-11-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you will come to the cinema on Friday. You say yes, unless you have a lot of work at the office.
b2-11-04.prompt: Tell Meg that you will come on Friday and name the one exception.
cues: Say that you will come on Friday
b2-11-04.target: Voy al cine el viernes, excepto que tenga mucho trabajo en la oficina.
b2-11-04.english: I am going to the cinema on Friday, unless I have a lot of work at the office.
b2-11-04.canDo: I can name the one exception that would change a plan with a menos que, a no ser que, salvo que and excepto que.

b2-11-05.title: Communicative Challenge: If I Am Not Mistaken
b2-11-05.scenario: You are Carlos. At the office you want to check the time of a meeting. You think it is at ten, but you are not sure.
b2-11-05.prompt: Politely say what time you think the meeting is.
cues: Say that you may be mistaken
Say the time of the meeting
b2-11-05.target: Si no me equivoco, la reunión es a las diez.
b2-11-05.english: If I am not mistaken, the meeting is at ten.
b2-11-05.canDo: I can soften a statement or a request with si no me equivoco, si mal no recuerdo, si me permite and si no es molestia.

b2-11-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Book Written as a Diary
b2-11-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you know about the novel La tregua. You say that without the diary form we would not know Santomé through his own words.
b2-11-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what would be different if Benedetti had not written the novel as a diary.
cues: Say what Benedetti would not have done
Say what we would not know today
b2-11-consolidation.target: Si Benedetti no hubiera escrito la novela como diario, hoy no conoceríamos a Santomé por sus palabras.
b2-11-consolidation.english: If Benedetti had not written the novel as a diary, today we would not know Santomé through his own words.
b2-11-consolidation.canDo: I can say how a different past would change the present, and how a lasting trait would have changed the past.
